trust_boundaries: External SaaS / End User -> Ingress Layer
architecture_summary.operational_context: Cloud-native SaaS integration pipeline processing third-party webhooks and user API traffic.

threat_actors.name: External Cybercriminal
threat_actors.motivation: Data theft, financial gain, service disruption
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Malicious webhook payloads or stolen user OAuth access tokens
non_capabilities: No direct access to cloud infrastructure management console

threat_actors.name: Malicious Insider
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Compromised developer credentials or compromised service accounts within the Integration Layer
non_capabilities: No administrative access to external third-party SaaS provider

attack_paths.impact: Injection of forged webhooks and unauthorized events directly into Event Queue
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Public webhook endpoints without cryptographic signature validation are vulnerable to request spoofing.

attack_paths.technique_name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token
attack_paths.impact: Account takeover and unauthorized invocation of integration downstream workflows
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Stolen or leaked user access tokens can be reused against the OAuth Proxy.

attack_paths.entry_point: Direct flow from Webhook Receiver to Event Queue
attack_paths.impact: Resource exhaustion and denial of service due to lack of rate limiting on the Webhook ingress path
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Webhook Receiver bypasses the Rate Limiter when pushing to Event Queue.

attack_paths.entry_point: Data Transformer processing untrusted event payloads
attack_paths.impact: Corruption or unauthorized manipulation of confidential records stored in Integration DB
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: If input sanitization is insufficient in Transformer, malicious payloads corrupt database state.

attack_paths.impact: Modification or deletion of audit logs to conceal malicious processing activities
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires compromise of the Transformer component inside the Integration Layer trust zone.

attack_paths.entry_point: Internal network boundary between Ingress and Integration layers
attack_paths.impact: Interception of confidential payload data in transit across internal boundaries
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Attacker must already hold network positioning inside the cloud environment.

mitigations.control_name: OAuth Token Validation and Short Token Lifespans
Strict Input Schema Validation in Data Transformer
Mandatory mTLS and Encrypted Data In Transit

findings.severity_rationale: Missing HMAC signature validation on public Webhook Receiver permits unauthenticated event injection into Event Queue.
Webhook Receiver routes traffic directly to Event Queue without passing through Rate Limiter, exposing the system to denial of service.
Replay or abuse of hijacked OAuth tokens at the proxy layer can grant illegal access to downstream processing.
Insufficient payload validation in Data Transformer may result in invalid or malicious data written to Integration DB.
Audit logs could be modified if Transformer service credentials are over-privileged.
Unencrypted inter-service traffic could allow network sniffing within the integration network segment.
